cards.explanation: The answer is the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. God says to bring it "…to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before His tabernacle…" (Leviticus 17:4). Not wherever you happen to be standing, not wherever it's convenient. One address, and it's on the paperwork.

The word is bloodguilt, friends. God says, "…that man shall incur bloodguilt. He has shed blood and must be cut off from among his people." I think this one is heavy, so it's good to hear it plainly. It's the LORD's own wording, and He doesn't water it down.

The answer is the open fields. God says the Israelites will bring "…the sacrifices they have been offering in the open fields." to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting (Leviticus 17:5). The sacrifices were already happening, friends. The place is what changes.

The answer is goat demons. God says the Israelites "…must no longer offer their sacrifices to the goat demons to which they have prostituted themselves." Then He adds that this "…will be a permanent statute for them for the generations to come." (Leviticus 17:7). Permanent, friends. That's not a suggestion taped to the fridge.

The answer is True. God says if anyone from the house of Israel "…or any foreigner living among them…" offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice but doesn't bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, "…that man must be cut off from his people." (Leviticus 17:8-9). God names both the Israelite and the foreigner living among them. There's no side door.

The reason is that the life of the flesh is in the blood. God says, "For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you to make atonement for your souls upon the altar…" (Leviticus 17:11). He explains Himself here, and the reason is life. Hold onto that one, friends.

The answer is on the altar. God says He has given the blood "…to make atonement for your souls upon the altar; for it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul." (Leviticus 17:11). He gave it for that purpose, and He says so Himself.

The answer is to drain it and cover it with dirt. Out in the field, a hunter who catches a wild animal or bird that may be eaten "…must drain its blood and cover it with dirt." (Leviticus 17:13). That goes for an Israelite and for a foreigner living among them. Two steps, and God doesn't skip either one. I've followed recipes with less clear instructions than that, and mine had pictures!

The answer is to wash his clothes and bathe with water. God says the person "…must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening; then he will be clean." (Leviticus 17:15). Both parts are required, friends, the clothes and the bath. It covers someone native or foreign.

The answer is False, friends. Here's what the text says: he "…will be unclean until evening; then he will be clean." (Leviticus 17:15). It happens after he washes his clothes and bathes with water. No seven days anywhere in the verse.
